evidence.reason: `durable_directory` intends to recover entries an earlier call may have created without persisting their parents (see the comment at lines 363-365), but the recovery branch is only one level deep. When the target already exists (e.g. `base/outbox/pending`), `created` is empty and the loop fsyncs only `directory.parent` (`outbox`), so `outbox`'s own entry in `base` is never persisted. The scenario is reachable: creating `base/outbox/pending` fsyncs outbox, then base, then base's parent; if the `base` fsync fails the call aborts before base's parent is synced, and a retry sees all directories present and skips those ancestors. Subsequent `atomic()`/`locked()` calls into `pending` then fsync only `outbox`, so writes succeed while `outbox` (and everything under it) can still be lost on a crash. The fix is local: in the recovery path, walk the ancestor chain and fsync each ancestor's parent, not just the target's immediate parent. This is a correctness repair to existing durability intent, not a new requirement, and does not need owner judgment; the added fsyncs are part of the same declared guarantee.
